master_table.notes: CIC is 4.4x larger in flow volume.
UNSW Backdoor spans multiple protocols; CIC Bot is IRC C&C traffic.
Natural precision is not directly comparable; standardized pi=0.0306 used.
UNSW includes one-hot protocol categoricals; CIC is purely numeric flow statistics.
Supervised ensemble generalized completely on UNSW Backdoor, but failed on CIC Bot.
CIC stacking maintains drastically lower operational false alarm load.
Derived comparison metric per Blueprint Section 4.5.
Both datasets confirm severe anomaly suppression at mu+3sigma due to heavy-tail variance.
Low benign FPR achieved at the expense of missing >99% of zero-day attacks.
Isolation Forest mirrors AE anomaly blindness on zero-day attack manifolds.
OR-fusion yields negligible rescue (<2%) across both benchmark datasets.

master_table.metric_description: Operational Cost (Extra False Alarms on Control)
master_table.notes: Rescue benefit is heavily outweighed by the false alarm triage burden.
Removing shortcut features does not materially alter RF Macro-F1 (|Delta| < 0.01).
Strong in-distribution performance across both datasets.
FT-Transformer identically replicates the dataset-specific zero-day behavior of trees.

mandatory_footnotes.footnote_a_prevalence: Natural evaluation prevalence differs substantially: UNSW-NB15 zero-day evaluation prevalence is 3.06% (583 attacks / 19,083 total flows in eval_control + protected_backdoor), whereas CIC-IDS-2017 prevalence is 9.53% (1,948 attacks / 20,448 total flows in EVAL_CONTROL + PROTECTED_BOT). Because natural precision is mathematically dependent on attack prevalence, direct cross-dataset precision comparisons must use the standardized derived metric at pi = 0.0306 per Blueprint Section 4.5.
mandatory_footnotes.footnote_b_protected_families: The protected zero-day attack classes have fundamentally different network behaviors: UNSW-NB15 Backdoor traffic spans diverse ports/protocols with strong feature overlap with other known attacks, enabling high supervised transfer. CIC-IDS-2017 Bot traffic (ARES botnet) consists of subtle IRC C&C channels whose flow statistics occupy benign-adjacent manifolds.
mandatory_footnotes.footnote_c_feature_representation: Feature modalities and dimensions differ: CIC-IDS-2017 uses K*=69 purely numeric flow counters. UNSW-NB15 published baselines used K=75 mutual-information selected features (EXP_MI_V1_1) including one-hot protocol categoricals (proto, service, state), whereas the exploratory UNSW FT-Transformer baseline evaluated the top K=50 mutual-information selected features (EXP_MI_V1), which is the exact prefix of the 75-feature set.
mandatory_footnotes.footnote_d_resolution_limits: At the nominal matched-FPR budget alpha = 0.1%, the expected false alarm count on an 18,500-flow control set is 18.5 (< 20 expected false alarms), designating this budget as LOW_RESOLUTION per Blueprint Section 4.4.
